area: Vite 8 (Rolldown) build & bundle — chunk-control API verification and now-vs-Stage-6 adjudication

item_verdicts.title: Correct chunk-control API for vite@8.1 is build.rolldownOptions.output.codeSplitting — not manualChunks, not advancedChunks
item_verdicts.why: Attacked from five angles, all held. (1) Installed types — node_modules/rolldown/dist/shared/define-config-BhJ90aEv.d.mts EXISTS at the exact filename cited (rolldown 1.1.5, vite 8.1.5, both read from their package.json) and contains verbatim: `codeSplitting?: boolean | CodeSplittingOptions;` with `@default true`; `manualChunks?: ManualChunksFunction` marked `@deprecated Please use codeSplitting instead` with `Note that unlike Rollup, object form is not supported.` and `If manualChunks and codeSplitting are both specified, manualChunks option will be ignored.`; `advancedChunks?: {...}` marked `@deprecated` with the same ignored-when-both warning; and `type AdvancedChunksOptions = CodeSplittingOptions;` / `type AdvancedChunksGroup = CodeSplittingGroup;` both @deprecated. (2) CodeSplittingGroup shape verified field-by-field: name (string|fn), test (StringOrRegExp|fn), priority, minSize, maxSize, minShareCount, includeDependenciesRecursively — every field listed is real. (3) vite/dist/node/index.d.ts: `rollupOptions?: RolldownOptions;` carries `Alias to rolldownOptions / @deprecated Use rolldownOptions instead` — rename claim exact. (4) SOURCE spot-check https://vite.dev/guide/migration returns verbatim `"build.rollupOptions": renamed to "build.rolldownOptions"` and `The object form output.manualChunks option is not supported anymore. The function form output.manualChunks is deprecated.` plus `Rolldown has the more flexible codeSplitting option`. (5) https://rolldown.rs/reference/OutputOptions.codeSplitting is live and documents groups with name/test/priority/minSize. Strongest confirmation: I ran the removed form — object-form manualChunks HARD-FAILS on this repo's vite@8.1.5 with `Invalid type: Expected Function but received Object.` then `TypeError: manualChunks is not a function`.

item_verdicts.title: Now-fix: add a build section with chunkSizeWarningLimit ~1500 to silence the cosmetic 1360kB warning
item_verdicts.why: Reproduced live rather than trusted. Baseline `npx vite build` emits EXACTLY what PROBLEMS.md records: assets/index-DsRXxsrp.js, 1,360.08 kB, gzip 366.89 kB, plus the warning naming build.rolldownOptions.output.codeSplitting and build.chunkSizeWarningLimit. I then built with a config carrying only `build: { chunkSizeWarningLimit: 1500 }` (defineConfig from 'vitest/config', exactly as prescribed): same filename index-DsRXxsrp.js, same 1,360.08 kB / gzip 366.89 kB, and sha256 IDENTICAL to baseline (e8d00d92…d927307 both) — 'byte-identical bundle' is literally true. Warning gone. vite/dist/node/index.d.ts confirms `chunkSizeWarningLimit?: number` / `Adjust chunk size warning limit (in kB). @default 500`. Headroom arithmetic checks: 1500 − 1360.08 = 139.92 ≈ claimed ~140 kB. The 'gate stays green' claim is understated — .githooks/pre-commit runs BUILD_CMD="npm run -s typecheck", TEST_CMD, LINT_CMD and never invokes `vite build`, so the warning could never gate a commit. RESUME_HERE.md line 215 verbatim: `- Phaser bundle 1.2 MB → code-split at Stage 6.` under '## Spark / backlog' — the cited deferral exists as quoted.

item_verdicts.title: Phaser vendor chunk via codeSplitting.groups — snippet verified working, but KEEP it at Stage 6 per the backlog
item_verdicts.why: The snippet and every number survive exactly — I ran it. `codeSplitting: { groups: [{ name: 'phaser', test: /node_modules[\\/]phaser[\\/]/, priority: 10 }] }` under build.rolldownOptions.output builds clean on vite@8.1.5 and emits phaser-mnkpczUE.js 1,198.00 kB / gzip 319.08 and index-CT0WDKnF.js 161.47 kB / gzip 48.04 — the research's figures to the byte. 'Limit raise needed WITH the split anyway' also verified: the 500 kB warning still fires on the split build. Runtime reasoning holds: grep shows ten static top-level `import Phaser from 'phaser'` across src/ and ZERO dynamic `import(`, so both chunks load at startup. The strictExecutionOrder caveat is real and correctly attributed — the live rolldown page warns verbatim 'manual code splitting can change the behavior of the application if side effects are triggered before the corresponding modules are actually used' and points to output.strictExecutionOrder. One defect: the stated output is incomplete.
item_verdicts.correction: The split build emits THREE assets, not two: assets/phaser-[hash].js 1,198.00 kB (gzip 319.08), assets/index-[hash].js 161.47 kB (gzip 48.04), AND assets/rolldown-runtime-[hash].js 0.56 kB (gzip 0.36) — a shared runtime chunk Rolldown injects only once splitting is on. index.html also grows 0.77 kB → 0.93 kB because it now references the extra scripts. Stage 6 should expect a 3-file chunk graph and re-check any preload/cache rules against it. Separately: the installed rolldown d.mts documents strictExecutionOrder only as 'Lets modules be executed in the order they are declared' plus a bundle-size warning — the side-effect-reordering rationale comes from the rolldown.rs docs page, not the type annotations.

item_verdicts.title: REJECT any config written against output.advancedChunks (the batch-1 doc's likely guess)
item_verdicts.why: The REJECT itself is unimpeachable and rests on primary evidence I re-read: the installed define-config-BhJ90aEv.d.mts marks advancedChunks `@deprecated Please use codeSplitting instead`, aliases `type AdvancedChunksOptions = CodeSplittingOptions`, and states advancedChunks is ignored when codeSplitting is also set; vite.dev/guide/migration indeed never names advancedChunks as current API. Two things are wrong at the edges, both checkable in seconds. (a) 'the batch-1 doc's likely guess' is a GUESS and it is wrong — docs/research/2026-08-05-improvements-research.md §12 (line ~496) proposes object-form `manualChunks: { phaser: ['phaser'], game: ['./src/main.ts'] }`, NOT advancedChunks. The researcher had the file in the repo and did not open it. (b) The issue-status framing is stale: vitejs/vite#21414 is CLOSED, not an open pending tracker. Both errors cut in the safe direction — the doc correction is MORE urgent than implied, since advancedChunks would merely be deprecated-but-working whereas the doc's actual snippet now hard-crashes the build.
item_verdicts.correction: Two fixes. (1) Drop 'the batch-1 doc's likely guess' — docs/research/2026-08-05-improvements-research.md §12 proposes object-form manualChunks, and that form is not merely deprecated but FATAL on vite@8.1.5: I ran it and got `Warning: Invalid output options (1 issue found) - For the "manualChunks". Invalid type: Expected Function but received Object.` then `error during build: TypeError: manualChunks is not a function` (build failed, no dist emitted). §12's snippet must be rewritten to the item-3 codeSplitting form before anyone copies it — a build-breaking correction, not a stylistic one. While there, §12 also writes `import { defineConfig } from 'vite'`, which if pasted over the repo's vite.config.ts would silently delete the vitest `test` block. (2) vitejs/vite#21414 is CLOSED (created 2026-01-15T01:04:43Z, closed 2026-01-24T09:24:46Z; body checkbox 'Outdated', body text 'After https://github.com/rolldown/rolldown/issues/7895 is done') — describe it as a closed docs ticket confirming the deprecation, not as work still 'pending'. It is also fully readable via `gh issue view 21414 --repo vitejs/vite --json title,state,createdAt,closedAt,body`, contrary to the dead_ends note.

overall_note: Strong batch — 2 CONFIRMED, 2 WEAKENED, 0 REFUTED, and both weakenings are peripheral (an omitted third build artifact; a wrong guess about a file sitting in the repo, plus a stale issue status). Every load-bearing technical claim reproduced under attack: I ran four real builds (baseline, chunkSizeWarningLimit-only, codeSplitting.groups, and object-form manualChunks) on the repo's actual vite@8.1.5 / rolldown 1.1.5, and every size, gzip figure and hash quoted came back exact — including a sha256 match proving the 'byte-identical bundle' claim literally true, not approximately. SOURCES: two A-grade URLs spot-checked with WebFetch (vite.dev/guide/migration, rolldown.rs/reference/OutputOptions.codeSplitting) plus the GitHub issue via gh — all live, all saying what was attributed to them; no fabricated or dead URLs. REPO: PROBLEMS.md problem 1, RESUME_HERE.md line 215 backlog row, vite.config.ts's vitest-only shape, package.json versions, and .githooks/pre-commit all match the research's description; no ALREADY_DONE items were claimed, and the single REJECT's cited invariant (the installed d.mts deprecation) is real. LEDGER: N/A by absence — this batch cites ZERO COMBAT_MEASUREMENTS.md rows, and grep for bundle/vite/chunk across the ledger returns nothing, so neither §00b nor the new 2026-08-12 'Verify-pass corrections' block in §S24-H (entirely combat geometry: HEAVY band 146–~275, point-blank 17 dmg on draw, dash constant-speed ~616 px/s, run core 573–685 px/s) touches anything here. Housekeeping: my three temporary verify configs were deleted and `git status` is back to its pre-verification state (only `?? PROBLEMS.md` untracked); test builds went to the scratchpad, repo dist/ untouched. Actionable residue for the parent: item 4's correction upgrades the batch-1 doc fix from 'tidy the API name' to 'fix a snippet that crashes the build'.
